query: What is the PK blood sampling timepoint after the start of infusion for the 2-hour post-dose sample?
response:
According to the protocol, the 2-hour post-dose blood sample corresponds to the **end of infusion**, as explicitly noted in the sampling schedule: samples are collected at "0.5, 1, 2 **(end of infusion)**, 6, 48..." hours after the start of administration (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p51). This applies both at the 1st dose and at the 6th dose time points.

Additionally, the acceptable time window for samples collected between **2 h and 12 h post-dosing** is defined as 'theoretical timepoint ±10 min' (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p51), which would apply to the 2-hour (end of infusion) sample boundary.

response:
The screening endoscopy should be performed **-35 to -6 days prior to Randomisation** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p.49). Additionally, endoscopy conducted within **2 months before Randomisation is acceptable** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p.49).

This is also reflected in the inclusion criteria, which states that the endoscopy subscore ≥2 must be obtained **during Day -35 to Day -6 prior to Randomisation** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p.34).

It is worth noting that a version change note (Version 1.1) clarifies that **endoscopy results obtained within 60 to 35 days prior to Randomisation may not be reliable as baseline** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p.95).

response:
This protocol uses a **Safety Review Committee (SRC)** — not a Data Safety Monitoring Committee (DSMC) — to oversee safety data.

The protocol defines the SRC as follows:

> "The SRC is an expert advisory group commissioned and charged with the responsibility of evaluating, primarily, cumulative safety data at regular intervals. The SRC will review blinded data and provide recommendations to the Sponsor based on their evaluation." (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 29)

During the trial, the SRC will "periodically review safety data, evaluate any safety concerns, and make recommendations to the Sponsor regarding trial conduct and possible trial modifications" and will comprise "at least a medical monitor, a physician and a pharmacologist." (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 29)

Importantly, the change from DSMC to SRC was a deliberate amendment documented in **Appendix 4 (Version 1.1 changes)**:

> "It is more appropriate to use SRC rather than DSMC as the name of the committee, since the purpose of the committee is to review safety data." (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 93)

The abbreviation list also confirms that **SRC = Safety Review Committee** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p. 19).

response:
## Total Infusion Sessions and Duration

A patient enrolled in this trial will receive **6 total infusion sessions** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p40), administered over a **12-week Treatment Period** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p43).

### Key Details:
- **Dosing schedule:** TJ301 or placebo is administered as i.v. infusions **every 2 weeks (Q2W)** (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p40)
- **Specific administration days:** Days 0, 14, 28, 42, 56, and 70 (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p26)
- **Infusion volume:** 290 mL per infusion (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p40)
- **Infusion duration:** 2 hours per session (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p40)
- **Post-infusion monitoring:** 3 hours after the 1st and 2nd infusions; 1 hour after remaining infusions (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p40)

Following the final infusion (Day 70), patients then enter a **3-week Safety Follow-up Period** extending to Day 105 (Protocol_Ulcerative Colitis.pdf, p43).

sources.exactText: The IMP will be administered as i.v. infusions every 2 weeks for 12 weeks (i.e. 6 infusions in total). An infusion volume of 290 mL will be used. The infusion time will be 2 hours. Following the first and second i.v. infusion, the patient will be monitored for infusion reactions at the site for three hours after infusion. For the remaining infusions, the patient will be monitored for one hour post-infusion only.
